title: Tag the stuck valve from the flow indicators
instruction: Two pneumatic panels each have one grey valve stuck shut and every other valve open. Dark blue lines are pipes from the blue supply. Outlet indicators show green for flow and black for no flow. Set one red tag on top of each panel's stuck valve.
context: Launch pads and test stands are fed by ground-support pneumatic panels. When some outlets lose pressure, a technician reads the line diagram on the panel face and applies the single-fault rule: find the one component whose failure explains every dead outlet without killing a live one, then hang a red danger tag on it before work starts. Each panel draws its pipe tree from a blue supply in dark blue lines, with outlet indicators green for flow and black for none. Nothing is probed or measured, so the fault must be inferred from the drawing. The panels differ: on the left the fault sits mid-tree above a junction feeding two dead outlets; on the right it is a leaf whose dead outlet sits nearer another valve, and the valve above its junction would also kill a live outlet. The main valve, the valve nearest a dead outlet, the valve nearest the tag and the valve farthest from the supply each score 0 on both panels. Earth gravity on a bench; no gas is simulated.
setup: Station table, both arms working, each in front of its own base. Table coordinates in metres: x forward from the line through the arm bases, y left from the midline; the bases are at y = +0.305 (left) and -0.305 (right). All objects are rigid matte boxes with one shared friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). Fixed, one panel per arm: a white (sRGB 0.92, 0.92, 0.90) board 260 x 240 x 6 mm (x, y, z) flat on the table, centred at (0.250, 0.305) and (0.250, -0.305). Standing on each board: a blue (sRGB 0.15, 0.35, 0.75) supply bottle 30 x 30 x 24 mm; grey (sRGB 0.55, 0.55, 0.57) valves 30 x 30 x 18 mm; outlet indicators 30 x 30 x 3 mm, green (sRGB 0.15, 0.75, 0.25) for flow or black (sRGB 0.10, 0.10, 0.10) for none; and dark blue (sRGB 0.10, 0.20, 0.55) line strips, the pipes, 10 mm wide and 3 mm tall, each along x or y on the line through two block centres, face to face, a branch butting against the side of the strip it leaves. Left centres: supply (0.150, 0.380), V1 (0.200, 0.380), V2 (0.300, 0.380), outlet O1 green (0.350, 0.380), V3 (0.250, 0.330), V4 (0.300, 0.280), O2 black (0.350, 0.280), V5 (0.250, 0.230), O3 black (0.200, 0.230). Left lines: supply, V1, V2, O1 along y = 0.380, junction J1 at x = 0.250; J1 to V3 to V5 along x = 0.250, junction J2 at y = 0.280; J2 to V4 to O2 along y = 0.280; V5 to O3 along y = 0.230. Right centres: supply (0.150, -0.230), V1 (0.200, -0.230), V2 (0.350, -0.230), V3 (0.300, -0.280), V4 (0.250, -0.330), O1 black (0.300, -0.380), O2 green (0.350, -0.330), O3 green (0.250, -0.380). Right lines: supply, V1, V2 along y = -0.230, J1 at x = 0.250; J1 to V4 to O3 along x = 0.250; V2 to O2 along x = 0.350, J2 at y = -0.280, with no valve between J2 and O2; J2 to V3 along y = -0.280; V3 to O1 along x = 0.300. The names are for this text only; nothing on the panels is labelled. Blocks stand at least 20 mm apart and 15 mm inside the board edge; every valve top is 24 mm above the table. Loose: two red (sRGB 0.85, 0.10, 0.10) tags, boxes 30 x 30 x 24 mm, 20 g, standing square on the table at (0.150, 0.110) and (0.150, -0.110), 60 mm inboard of each board. To build it: cut the boards from 6 mm white sheet, print or cut the blocks, glue them and 10 x 3 mm dark blue strip to the boards at the stated centres, tape the boards to the table, and print the tags in PLA to 20 g and paint them red.
scoring: End state only, judged after the arms have released and moved clear, from a top photo, a tape measure and a phone level. A tag is on a valve when it is at rest (under 10 mm/s and 0.5 rad/s), flat on any face (some face within 10 degrees of level), with its lowest point within 4 mm of that valve's top (24 mm above the table) and its centre within 12 mm of the valve's centre seen from above. Each panel scores 0.5 when a tag is on its stuck valve and no tag is on any other valve of that panel; otherwise that panel scores 0. The task score is the sum, so 0, 0.5 or 1.0. Either tag may serve either panel. Success, which ends the trial, is both panels at 0.5, held for 1 s. The stuck valve is V3 on both panels, the only valve whose closure explains the indicators: on the left it cuts the black O2 and O3 and spares the green O1; on the right it cuts the black O1 and spares the green O2 and O3. Reference outcomes, each 0 for that panel: V1 on either panel, which also kills a green outlet; left V2, which kills only the green O1; left V4 or V5, each of which explains one black outlet of two; right V2, which also kills the green O2; right V4, which kills the green O3. A random valve is right one time in five on the left and one in four on the right, so a random policy reaches 1.0 one time in 20. Copying one panel's answer to the same or the mirrored spot on the other panel finds a wrong valve or none. Two tags on valves of one panel score 0 for that panel, even if one is on the stuck valve, and the other panel then has no tag. A tag stacked on another tag, tilted more than 10 degrees, held more than 4 mm above a valve, still moving, on the board, an indicator, a line, the supply bottle, the table or the floor is on no valve. The start state scores 0. A tag cannot be pushed up onto a valve: the valve tops stand 24 mm above the table and the panels are fixed. In simulation the tests use each tag's centre and quaternion (its lowest point from its centre, size and orientation), not its axis-aligned bounds, and an exact 12 mm or 4 mm counts. Release is inferred from a tag being at rest, so a tag held motionless on a valve would also count; on real arms the photo is taken after the grippers have opened and moved clear. The panels are fixed in simulation; on the real rig, a trial in which any board or block moves more than 5 mm from its mark scores 0.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Stand the two tags back on their marks at (0.150, 0.110) and (0.150, -0.110), square to the table edges; the panels do not move.
fidelity: Approximate: each panel is a flat line-diagram board of rigid blocks and strips on the bench, not an upright panel with plumbed valves; no gas, pressure or valve mechanism is simulated, and the indicators are fixed colours, not live gauges; a tag is a 20 g block set on the valve top, not a card hung from its handle. Rigid primitives with one shared friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic), Earth gravity on a bench, where this troubleshooting is done.
